sections.subtitle: Basic Coordinating Conjunctions
sections.content: Y (and): connects words, phrases, or clauses. 'Juan y María' (Juan and María), 'Como y bebo' (I eat and drink). IMPORTANT: Changes to E before words starting with i- or hi-: 'padre e hijo' (father and son), 'español e inglés' (Spanish and English). O (or): presents alternatives. 'Café o té' (Coffee or tea). IMPORTANT: Changes to U before words starting with o- or ho-: 'siete u ocho' (seven or eight), 'mujer u hombre' (woman or man). PERO (but): introduces contrast. 'Es caro pero bueno' (It's expensive but good). SINO (but rather): contrast after negation, correcting previous statement. 'No es verde sino azul' (It's not green but (rather) blue). Use SINO only after negative statements to correct/replace info. PORQUE (because): gives reason. '¿Por qué estudias? Porque quiero aprender' (Why do you study? Because I want to learn).

sections.subtitle: Pero vs Sino & Double Negatives
sections.content: PERO vs SINO: PERO = general contrast, can follow affirmative or negative. 'Es inteligente pero perezoso' (He's smart but lazy - affirmative + contrast). 'No es fácil, pero es posible' (It's not easy, but it's possible - negative + contrast). SINO = correction after negation, replaces the negated element. 'No es médico sino abogado' (He's not a doctor but (rather) a lawyer - corrects profession). 'No quiero café sino té' (I don't want coffee but tea - replaces drink). Remember: SINO corrects what was just negated. NI...NI (neither...nor): double negative construction. 'No tengo ni tiempo ni dinero' (I have neither time nor money / I don't have time nor money). Can also use: 'Ni Juan ni María vienen' (Neither Juan nor María is coming). Spanish embraces double/multiple negatives: 'No veo nada nunca' (I never see anything - literally 'I don't see nothing never').

sections.subtitle: Subordinating Conjunctions: Basic & Temporal
sections.content: QUE (that): introduces subordinate clauses. 'Sé que estudias' (I know that you study), 'Creo que sí' (I think so). Often required in Spanish where 'that' is optional in English. SI (if): introduces conditional clauses. 'Si llueve, no voy' (If it rains, I won't go). Note: si (if) vs sí (yes) - accent matters! CUANDO (when): time relationship. 'Cuando llegues, llama' (When you arrive, call). With future meaning, use subjunctive: 'Cuando tenga tiempo...' (When I have time...). MIENTRAS (while): simultaneous actions. 'Mientras cocino, él limpia' (While I cook, he cleans). Can also mean 'as long as' with subjunctive: 'Mientras tengas salud...' (As long as you have health...). ANTES DE QUE (before): requires subjunctive. 'Antes de que salgas' (Before you leave). DESPUÉS DE QUE (after): may take subjunctive or indicative depending on whether action is completed.

sections.subtitle: Subordinating Conjunctions: Concessive & Purpose
sections.content: AUNQUE (although/even though): concession. With indicative for known facts: 'Aunque llueve, voy' (Although it's raining, I'm going - it IS raining). With subjunctive for possibility: 'Aunque llueva, voy' (Even if it rains, I'm going - it might rain). PARA QUE (so that/in order that): purpose, requires subjunctive. 'Hablo despacio para que entiendas' (I speak slowly so that you understand). Purpose = subjunctive always! COMO (as/like/since): comparison or reason. 'Como estaba cansado, dormí' (Since/As I was tired, I slept). COMO SI (as if): hypothetical comparison, requires imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive. 'Habla como si supiera todo' (He speaks as if he knew everything - but he doesn't). SIN QUE (without): requires subjunctive. 'Salió sin que lo viera' (He left without me seeing him). A MENOS QUE (unless): requires subjunctive. 'No voy a menos que vengas' (I won't go unless you come). CON TAL DE QUE (provided that): requires subjunctive. 'Voy con tal de que pagues' (I'll go provided that you pay).

sections.subtitle: Connectors: Sequencing & Addition
sections.content: SEQUENCING CONNECTORS: Order events or ideas. PRIMERO (first/firstly): 'Primero, lee el texto' (First, read the text). LUEGO / DESPUÉS (then/afterwards): 'Luego, responde las preguntas' (Then, answer the questions). FINALMENTE / POR FIN / AL FINAL (finally/at last): 'Finalmente, revisamos' (Finally, we review). Also: ENTONCES (then/so), MÁS TARDE (later), ANTES (before), AHORA (now). ADDITION CONNECTORS: Add information. ADEMÁS (besides/furthermore/in addition): 'Además, es muy caro' (Besides, it's very expensive). TAMBIÉN (also/too): 'Yo también voy' (I'm going too). TAMPOCO (neither/not either): used in negative contexts. 'No me gusta. A mí tampoco' (I don't like it. Me neither). 'Tampoco como carne' (I don't eat meat either). Y TAMBIÉN (and also), NI SIQUIERA (not even): 'Ni siquiera lo intentó' (He didn't even try it).

sections.subtitle: Connectors: Contrast & Cause-Effect
sections.content: CONTRAST CONNECTORS: Show opposition or unexpected results. SIN EMBARGO (however/nevertheless): 'Es difícil; sin embargo, lo intentaré' (It's difficult; however, I'll try). NO OBSTANTE (nevertheless/nonetheless): formal alternative to sin embargo. EN CAMBIO (on the other hand/instead): 'Él trabaja; en cambio, ella estudia' (He works; she, on the other hand, studies). MIENTRAS QUE (whereas/while): contrast between two situations. 'Yo estudio, mientras que tú descansas' (I study, whereas you rest). A PESAR DE (in spite of): 'A pesar del frío, salimos' (In spite of the cold, we went out). CAUSE & EFFECT CONNECTORS: Show logical relationships. POR ESO (that's why/for that reason): 'Estudié mucho; por eso aprobé' (I studied a lot; that's why I passed). POR LO TANTO (therefore): 'Es tarde; por lo tanto, debemos irnos' (It's late; therefore, we should leave). ASÍ QUE (so/therefore): less formal. 'Tengo hambre; así que comeré' (I'm hungry; so I'll eat). PORQUE (because - as clause), YA QUE / PUESTO QUE (since/because - more formal).

questions.question: 'Español e inglés' or 'Español y inglés' - which is correct?

answers.text: Español e inglés (y → e before i-/hi-)
Español y inglés (y never changes)
Both are equally correct
Neither is correct

questions.hint: Y changes to E before words starting with i- or hi- (español E inglés).

questions.question: 'Siete o ocho' or 'Siete u ocho' - which is correct?

answers.text: Siete u ocho (o → u before o-/ho-)
Siete o ocho (o never changes)
Both are equally correct
Neither is correct

questions.hint: O changes to U before words starting with o- or ho- (siete U ocho).

questions.question: 'Padre e hijo' - Why 'e' instead of 'y'?

answers.text: Because 'hijo' starts with hi-, y changes to e
Because 'padre' ends with e
Random variation
Both y and e work equally

questions.hint: Y → E before words starting with i- or hi-. Hijo starts with hi-.

questions.question: 'No es verde sino azul' - Why 'sino' not 'pero'?

answers.text: Sino corrects/replaces after negation (not green BUT blue)
Pero is never used after negation
Sino and pero are always interchangeable
Sino is used with colors only

questions.hint: SINO corrects the negated element. It's not green but (rather) blue - replacing color.

questions.question: 'Es caro pero bueno' - Why 'pero' not 'sino'?

answers.text: Pero shows general contrast (expensive BUT good)
Sino is only after negatives
This should use sino because of contrast
Random choice between pero and sino

questions.hint: PERO = general contrast. SINO = correction after negation only. 'Es caro' is affirmative, so use pero.

questions.question: 'No quiero café sino té' vs 'No es fácil, pero es posible' - What's the difference?

answers.text: Sino replaces café with té; pero adds contrasting info
Both use pero for contrast
Both use sino after negation
No difference, interchangeable

questions.hint: SINO = replacement/correction after negation. PERO = additional contrasting information.

questions.question: What does 'No tengo ni tiempo ni dinero' mean?

answers.text: I have neither time nor money
I have either time or money
I have both time and money
I have only time, not money

questions.hint: Ni...ni = neither...nor. Spanish uses double negatives: no + ni...ni.

questions.question: 'Creo que sí' - Why is 'que' needed?

answers.text: Que introduces the subordinate clause (that you do)
Que is optional, like English 'that'
Que means 'yes' here
Random usage

questions.hint: QUE (that) is typically required in Spanish to introduce clauses, unlike English where 'that' is often optional.

questions.question: 'Si llueve, no voy' - What does this mean?

answers.text: If it rains, I won't go
Yes, it rains and I don't go
When it rains, I always go
It's raining, but I go

questions.hint: SI (without accent) = if (conditional). Sí (with accent) = yes.

questions.question: 'Mientras cocino, él limpia' means...

answers.text: While I cook, he cleans (simultaneous actions)
Before I cook, he cleans
After I cook, he cleans
If I cook, he cleans

questions.hint: MIENTRAS = while (simultaneous actions happening at the same time).

questions.question: 'Cuando llegues, llama' - Why subjunctive 'llegues'?

answers.text: Future/uncertain event with cuando requires subjunctive
Cuando always requires subjunctive
This is an error, should be 'llegas'
Llama requires subjunctive in the cuando clause

questions.hint: CUANDO + subjunctive when referring to future/uncertain events. When you arrive (future), call.

questions.question: 'Antes de que salgas' - Why is 'que' needed?

answers.text: Antes de que is a compound conjunction requiring que
Que is optional with antes de
Que is only for emphasis
This should be 'antes de salgas' without que

questions.hint: Before a conjugated verb, use ANTES DE QUE (before). Always requires subjunctive.

questions.question: 'Aunque llueve, voy' vs 'Aunque llueva, voy' - What's the difference?

answers.text: Llueve = it IS raining (fact); llueva = it might rain (possibility)
No difference, both mean the same
Llueve is past, llueva is present
Llueva is an error

questions.hint: AUNQUE + indicative = known fact. AUNQUE + subjunctive = possibility/hypothetical.

questions.question: 'Hablo despacio para que entiendas' - Why subjunctive 'entiendas'?

answers.text: Para que (so that/purpose) always requires subjunctive
Para que sometimes uses subjunctive
This should be 'entiendes' in indicative
Despacio requires subjunctive in the para clause

questions.hint: PARA QUE (so that) = purpose, always requires subjunctive. I speak slowly SO THAT you understand.

questions.question: 'Habla como si supiera todo' - What does 'como si' mean?

answers.text: As if (he speaks as if he knew everything - but doesn't)
Since (he speaks since he knows everything)
When (he speaks when he knows everything)
Because (he speaks because he knows everything)

questions.hint: COMO SI = as if (hypothetical comparison). Always requires imperfect/pluperfect subjunctive.

questions.question: 'Salió sin que lo viera' - Why subjunctive 'viera'?

answers.text: Sin que (without) always requires subjunctive
Sin que never requires subjunctive
This should be 'veía' in imperfect indicative
Random usage

questions.hint: SIN QUE (without) always requires subjunctive. He left without me seeing him.

questions.question: What's the correct order? 'First, read. Then, write. Finally, review.'

answers.text: Primero, lee. Luego, escribe. Finalmente, revisa.
Finalmente, lee. Luego, escribe. Primero, revisa.
Además, lee. También, escribe. Tampoco, revisa.
Sin embargo, lee. Por eso, escribe. Aunque, revisa.

questions.hint: Sequencing: PRIMERO (first) → LUEGO (then) → FINALMENTE (finally).

questions.question: 'No me gusta. A mí tampoco.' What does 'tampoco' mean?

answers.text: Neither / Me neither (negative agreement)
Also / Me too (positive agreement)
Yes, me neither
However

questions.hint: TAMPOCO = neither/not either (negative contexts). Also = TAMBIÉN (positive contexts).

questions.question: 'Además, es muy caro' means...

answers.text: Besides/Furthermore/In addition, it's very expensive
However, it's very expensive
Therefore, it's very expensive
Although it's very expensive

questions.hint: ADEMÁS = besides/furthermore/in addition (adds information).

questions.question: 'Es difícil; sin embargo, lo intentaré' means...

answers.text: It's difficult; however, I'll try (contrast)
It's difficult; therefore, I'll try (cause-effect)
It's difficult; also, I'll try (addition)
It's difficult; first, I'll try (sequence)

questions.hint: SIN EMBARGO = however/nevertheless (shows contrast/unexpected result).

questions.question: 'Estudié mucho; por eso aprobé' means...

answers.text: I studied a lot; that's why I passed (cause → effect)
I studied a lot; however, I passed (contrast)
I studied a lot; also, I passed (addition)
I studied a lot; although I passed

questions.hint: POR ESO = that's why/for that reason (shows cause-effect relationship).

questions.question: 'Tengo hambre; así que comeré' - What does 'así que' mean?

answers.text: So / Therefore (cause-effect, informal)
However (contrast)
Also (addition)
Although (concession)

questions.hint: ASÍ QUE = so/therefore (less formal than por lo tanto). Shows cause-effect.

questions.question: 'Yo estudio, mientras que tú descansas' - What does 'mientras que' show?

answers.text: Contrast/opposition (whereas - I study while you rest)
Simultaneous identical actions
Cause and effect
Sequence of events

questions.hint: MIENTRAS QUE = whereas/while (contrast between two different situations).

questions.question: 'No voy a menos que vengas' - What does 'a menos que' mean?

answers.text: Unless (I won't go unless you come)
Because (I won't go because you come)
Although (I won't go although you come)
So that (I won't go so that you come)

questions.hint: A MENOS QUE = unless (always requires subjunctive). Expresses exception/condition.
